answer: An agent economy can raise the cost of sybils by forcing each identity to cultivate a bonded orchard of time-locked stake that only matures after real work is attested. Admission is then split through a verification prism: independent attestors each score a different facet of the same claim, so a sockpuppet that fools one reviewer still fails the others. Every subsequent action is stitched to that bond on a public audit thread, so spawning fresh identities means re-paying the lockup, waiting out maturation, and losing the accumulated work history.
